---
title: "How to compute features from LFPack archives and NumPy arrays"
---

Two sources carry **only the LF band**, already preprocessed:

| Source | Calculator | Typical input |
|---|---|---|
| An lfpack archive | `LFPackFeatureCalculator` | The [compressed LFP](load-lfp-features.qmd) IBL publishes, or one you packed yourself |
| An array in memory | `NumpyArrayFeatureCalculator` | LF you already loaded and resampled, from any format |

Both compute the `lf` and `csd` families. `ap` and `waveforms` need the AP band, which
neither source has. Everything else, including windows, options, on-disk layout and
aggregation, works as on the [SpikeGLX page](compute-features-spikeglx.qmd).

## Two options both sources need

The LF in an lfpack archive has already been high-pass filtered, common-average
referenced, bad-channel interpolated, decimated (to ~250 Hz) and Cadzow-denoised. The
NumPy calculator is meant for LF prepared the same way. So tell the pipeline **not** to
redo that preprocessing at the wrong sample rate:

```python
from ephysatlas.feature_calculators import (
    CsdParams,
    FeatureComputationOptions,
    FeatureParams,
)

options = FeatureComputationOptions(
    features_to_compute=["lf", "csd"],
    skip_lf_destripe=True,                                   # no destriping
    feature_params=FeatureParams(
        csd=CsdParams(decimate=1, denoise=False)             # no CSD decimation or denoising
    ),
)
```

Without `skip_lf_destripe=True`, destriping fails on 250 Hz data:

```text
ValueError: Digital filter critical frequencies must be 0 < Wn < fs/2 (fs=250.0 -> fs/2=125.0)
```

## From an lfpack archive

```python
from ephysatlas.feature_calculators import LFPackFeatureCalculator, SnippetWindow

calc = LFPackFeatureCalculator(
    "/data/lfp_aggregates/lf_compressed_v04_a07_default_all.h5",
    recording="00a824c0-e060-495f-9ebc-79c82fef4c67",   # the pid of one recording
)

print(calc.available_duration())   # (None, <seconds>): LF only

result = calc.compute_snippet(
    SnippetWindow(t_start=300.0, duration_ap=0.0, duration_lf=5.0), options
)
print(result.computed_features)    # ('lf', 'csd')
```

| argument | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `h5_file` | required | The archive |
| `recording` | `None` | Recording key: the pid. Required when the archive holds more than one recording, as the published ones do |
| `scale` | `0` | lfpack reconstruction scale (`0` = full quality) |
| `bin_channels` | `1` | Adjacent electrodes summed per output channel |
| `name` | `recording`, else the file stem | Recording identifier, used as the `pid` in outputs |

The reader opens lazily, on first access. The channel table comes from the archive:
`channel`, `lateral_um`, `axial_um`, `labels` and `shank`, plus `x`, `y`, `z`, `atlas_id`
and `acronym` when the archive carries them.

The archive also records where the amplifier saturated:

```python
calc.saturation_times()   # DataFrame: start_sample, stop_sample, start_time, stop_time
calc.saturation_mask      # boolean, one value per LF sample
```

## From a NumPy array

```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from ephysatlas.feature_calculators import NumpyArrayFeatureCalculator

# lf: (n_channels, n_samples) in volts, already resampled to fs_lf
# x_um, y_um: lateral and axial position of each channel, in µm
channels = pd.DataFrame({
    "channel": np.arange(len(x_um)),
    "axial_um": y_um,
    "lateral_um": x_um,
    "shank": 0,
    "labels": 0,            # QC label per channel: 0 = good
})

calc = NumpyArrayFeatureCalculator(
    lf=lf,
    fs_lf=250.0,
    geometry={"x": x_um, "y": y_um},
    name="subject42_probe00",
    channel_metadata=channels,
)
result = calc.compute_snippet(
    SnippetWindow(t_start=2.0, duration_ap=0.0, duration_lf=2.0), options
)
```

`geometry` needs at least `x` and `y`. The derived keys (`sample_shift`, `shank`, `col`,
`row`) are filled with defaults. `t0` (default `0.0`) is the session time of the array's
first sample, for an array cut out of a longer recording.

`channel_metadata` is optional for a single snippet. Without it the calculator builds
`channel`, `axial_um`, `lateral_um` and `shank` from `geometry`. The aggregated route
below takes the bad-channel labels from its `labels` column, so pass it when you have
them.

## Many snippets, aggregated and denoised

The one call from the [SpikeGLX page](compute-features-spikeglx.qmd#many-snippets-from-one-recording)
works for both sources. Pass the same `options`:

```python
df = calc.compute_denoised_features(
    n_snippets=5, duration_ap=0.0, duration_lf=5.0, options=options
)
print(df.index.names)   # ['pid', 'channel']
```

The result is the per-channel, denoised table, with only the `lf` and `csd` columns. A
model that also needs `ap` and `waveforms` features cannot run on it.

::: {.callout-important}
## Channel labels come from the channel table

With destriping skipped, no channel QC labels are computed. Denoising takes them from the
channel table's `labels` column instead. A NumPy calculator without `channel_metadata`,
or an archive recording with no labels, logs `No channel_labels in the features: all
channels are labelled good (0)`, and bad channels are then denoised like good ones.
:::

## Troubleshooting

**`ValueError: Digital filter critical frequencies must be 0 < Wn < fs/2`** — the
options lack `skip_lf_destripe=True`.

**`ValueError: Snippets starting at ... overlap`** — the recording is too short for that
many snippets of that length. Choose the windows yourself; see
[many snippets from one recording](compute-features-spikeglx.qmd#many-snippets-from-one-recording).

**`ValueError: Multiple recordings in file, specify recording= from: [...]`** — the archive
holds several recordings; pass the pid as `recording=`. A pid the archive does not hold
raises `KeyError: Recording '...' not found. Available: [...]`.
